pages.title: The Farther Offshore, the Deeper
pages.text: Heading out from the coast, the farther from land you go, the deeper the ocean becomes.$(br)$(li)Within about 64 blocks: almost no extra cut; the shore stays shallow.$(li)About 64~384 blocks: the fastest drop, up to 22 blocks below the original seafloor.$(li)About 384~640 blocks: a little deeper, about 24 blocks in total.$(li)About 640~1150 blocks: the deepest stage, about 27 blocks in total.

pages.title: How Deep It Gets
pages.text: $(li)Ordinary ocean (continental shelf): seafloor around y=15~29, at most y=15.$(li)Ocean reefs stay shallow, with their outer edge sloping gradually toward deep water.$(li)Deep ocean plains: seafloor around y=-10~6, about 57~73 blocks below sea level.$(li)Ocean ridges, atolls, and volcanic arcs share the same deepening, so they never rise abruptly above the surrounding seafloor.

pages.title: Trenches
pages.text: Trenches have a deeper seafloor: past about 1180 blocks from land, the core drops once more, up to 20 blocks, and never pushes the seafloor below y=-30, with the axis bottoming out near y=-40.
